tour.overview:
No architect has shaped a city quite like Antoni Gaudí shaped Barcelona. Between the 1880s and his death in 1926 he filled it with buildings that look grown rather than built: façades like waves and bones, roofs like dragons' backs, a park of mosaic serpents, and a basilica still rising today. Seven of his works are listed together as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

This private day connects the great Gaudí sites with a licensed guide and a car, so you spend your energy looking rather than queuing or finding taxis. You start at the Sagrada Família with timed tickets, inside the forest of tree-like columns as the morning sun pours through the stained glass. You drive up to Park Güell for its mosaic terrace and views to the sea, then down Passeig de Gràcia to the façades of Casa Batlló and La Pedrera. After a lunch of Catalan tapas, you walk through the Gothic Quarter, where Roman walls, the medieval cathedral and quiet squares tell the story of Barcelona before Gaudí.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours
• Start and end: your hotel or the cruise terminal in Barcelona
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability, ticket times and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy; about 5 km of walking, some steps in Park Güell

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Sagrada Família (inside and the Nativity façade).
• Park Güell (Monumental Zone).
• Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) from Passeig de Gràcia.
• The Gothic Quarter and Barcelona Cathedral.

WHY THIS WORKS
Sagrada Família tickets sell out weeks ahead and come with a fixed time; we book them for the morning, when the light through the eastern windows is strongest, and plan the rest of the day around that slot.

WHO IT SUITS
First-time visitors, cruise passengers, families and anyone interested in architecture and design.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you want mountains and wine, choose our Montserrat day trip. If you want to go inside Casa Batlló or La Pedrera, we can add one instead of Park Güell.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The Sagrada Família is a church: shoulders and knees must be covered. Book as early as possible for spring, summer and holiday dates. Pickpockets are common in crowded places, so keep bags closed.

days.name: Sagrada Família, Park Güell, Passeig de Gràcia and the Gothic Quarter
days.description:
What to expect: Gaudí's greatest works and the medieval heart of Barcelona with a licensed guide, private car, tickets and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at about 8:45 and take you to the Sagrada Família, the basilica Gaudí took over in 1883 and worked on for the rest of his life. Outside, your guide reads the Nativity façade with you – the only one finished in his lifetime, carved with the birth of Christ, angels, animals and plants. Inside, the nave opens like a forest: columns branch like trees towards a ceiling of stars, and the stained glass throws blue and green light on one side and orange and red on the other. You learn how Gaudí used models of hanging chains to find his shapes, why the basilica is still unfinished, and how its central tower, dedicated to Jesus Christ, makes it the tallest church in the world. You can also visit the small museum and see Gaudí's tomb in the crypt through a window.

Your driver takes you up the hill to Park Güell, planned as a garden city for wealthy families and now a park. In the Monumental Zone you see the two gingerbread-like pavilions at the entrance, the mosaic salamander on the staircase, the Hypostyle Room of 86 columns, and the long serpentine bench covered in broken tiles, with views over the city to the sea. On the way back down you stop on Passeig de Gràcia to see Casa Batlló, with its balconies like masks and its roof like a dragon's back, and Casa Milà, known as La Pedrera, 'the stone quarry', with its waving stone façade and iron balconies like seaweed.

After lunch of Catalan tapas – pa amb tomàquet, croquetes, grilled vegetables and local cheese – you walk through the Gothic Quarter. Your guide shows you the remains of the Roman wall of Barcino, the Plaça del Rei where the Catholic Monarchs are said to have received Columbus, the narrow Carrer del Bisbe with its neo-Gothic bridge, and the Cathedral of the Holy Cross and Saint Eulàlia, whose cloister keeps 13 white geese, one for each year of the young martyr's life. Your driver takes you back to your hotel or ship at about 16:45.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:45 – Pick-up from your hotel or the cruise terminal.
09:15 – Sagrada Família (about 1 hour 45 minutes).
11:15 – Park Güell, Monumental Zone (about 1 hour 15 minutes).
12:45 – Casa Batlló and La Pedrera from Passeig de Gràcia.
13:30 – Lunch of Catalan tapas.
14:45 – Gothic Quarter and Barcelona Cathedral.
16:45 – Return to your hotel or ship.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Ticket times may change the order of the day; we confirm the plan with your booking.
• On Sunday mornings the Sagrada Família holds Mass; we visit later that day.
• Entry to Casa Batlló or La Pedrera can replace Park Güell on request.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, Sagrada Família and Park Güell tickets, lunch, bottled water, pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: Sagrada Família towers, Casa Batlló or La Pedrera entry, cathedral entry, drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability, ticket times and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Are the Sagrada Família tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes, timed entry tickets to the basilica are included. Tower access is extra and depends on availability.

faq.question: How far ahead should I book?
faq.answer: As early as possible: Sagrada Família tickets often sell out two to four weeks ahead in spring and summer.

faq.question: Is it suitable as a cruise shore excursion?
faq.answer: Yes. We pick you up at the cruise terminal and plan the day around your ship's times, with a guaranteed return.

faq.question: Can we go inside Casa Batlló or La Pedrera?
faq.answer: Yes, as a replacement for Park Güell or as an extra. Tell us when you book and we will reserve tickets.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes and clothes that cover shoulders and knees for the Sagrada Família and the cathedral.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, Catalan tapas in the old town. Vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options can be arranged.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love Park Güell's mosaics and the dragon-like Casa Batlló. We can shorten the walking.

faq.question: Is it suitable for wheelchair users?
faq.answer: Mostly. The Sagrada Família and Passeig de Gràcia are accessible; Park Güell has slopes and the Gothic Quarter has uneven paving. Tell us your needs.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no shopping stops on this tour unless you ask.

faq.question: Can we take photos inside the Sagrada Família?
faq.answer: Yes, without flash or tripods. Photos are not allowed during Mass.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: April to June and September to October. July and August are hot and very busy; winter is mild and quiet.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 72 hours before the tour; Sagrada Família tickets cannot be refunded after that. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
